title: Are the fractional parts of (3/2)^n dense?
premise_risks: Area is borderline: this is uniform distribution / Diophantine analysis rather than core dynamics.
Famous and extremely hard (low novelty). It should not be confused with the named Mahler Z-number problem, which is related but separate.
plain: Write down 3/2, 9/4, 27/8, ... and keep only the part after the decimal point. Numerically these fractional parts look uniformly spread over [0,1), but nobody can prove they even come arbitrarily close to every number in [0,1]. Prove that they do.
math: Prove that $\{ \{(3/2)^n\} : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is dense in $[0,1]$, where $\{t\} = t - \lfloor t \rfloor$.
